Messages.Body:
OK, I am not willing to give in on these guys, so...

If a Shock Troop vamp got hold of a Writ of Acceptance, would it be
considered a Caitiff?

My thinking is that in the Camerilla, there is no such thing as a
Clanless vampire. To be part of the Camerilla, they have to accept the
Traditions (denoted by the writ). All the "clanless" and "unalligned"
camerilla vamps are swept into the movement that is the Caitiff.
Therefore a clanless Sabbat vampire that became a Camerilla vampire
would be a Caitiff.

Whilst the closest equivalent of the caitiff in the Sabbat is the
Panders, they still have equal rights to other clans - such is the
nature of the Sabbat. The "Clanless" element of a Shock Troop vampire
demonstrates the fact that they are so newly embraced that they have no
idea about vampiric society - no one has told them and are not expected
to last! However, if a Shock Troop had time to be educated and was
accepted into the Camerilla (again denoted by the Writ of Acceptance),
surely it would follow that they would be accepted as a Caitiff.

So, whaddaya think LSJ?

Best regards

DH

Sent via Deja.com
http://www.deja.com/

I think the games should definitely be seperate entities BUT the World of
Darkness that White Wolf created needs to be adhered to only because it is
such a cool world. The mythology that White Wolf has created is fantastic...
even if you have no interest in playing the role-playing game.

I was actually a player of Jyhad long before I ever played the role-playing
game. I had NO interest in playing role-playing games, as I was totally
turned off of them by my experiences in early high-school with Dungeons and
Dragons. I picked up a few of the 'Clanbooks' for the clans I liked in
Jyhad, Brujah and Ventrue. I read them only because I wanted to find out
more about the universe Jyhad was made from. I fell in love. I eventually
started playing the role-playing games, though not very often (I still find
the majority of Vampire: the Masquerade players to be absolute losers who
play V:tM like D&D with fangs). However, I have about 50 or so of the 'rule'
books, which I read because the setting fascinates me. I love the concept of
'clans' of vampires... I love the idea of the 'secret societies' controlling
the world from the darkness... I love the whole 'uber-angst' feel of the
World of Darkness.

Jyhad is NOT the same game to be sure, but it does rely on that same set of
myths and in my opinion can learn from the RPG. Even as far as expansions
for Jyhad, the RPG is a great wealth of possibilities. The changes in the
meta-storyline that White Wolf has recently instituted, such as the Gangrel
leaving the Camarilla (and now apparently some Assamites have joined it!)
are interesting and definitely create possibilities for the cards. Whether
they would be good cards or not is questionable. A card that causes the
Gangrel to lose their membership in the Camarilla would be both a boon and
bane to Gangrel players... Primogen, Princes and Justicars lose their votes,
but Gangrel can now play cards for non-Camarilla (ok... bad example).
While it is not absolutely required for the cards to fall in line with the
ongoing changes to the WoD, I believe that the theme should remain loyal to
the mythos.

Ultimately, when you remove all card text flavour and reduce the game to
it's basic components, Jyhad could be about anything... gangsters in rival
families, sports teams, whatever. At some level, it is the theme of the game
that does appeal to us (or at least me). I love the fact that Jyhad is a
game full of intricate strategies and infinite complexities but I also love
the fact that it is about vampires... AND the World of Darkness
specifically.

As long as new cards are not broken, not wallpaper and don't take away from
the fun of playing this game... I say bring them on! Making the cards with a
flavour that follows the RPG makes more sense than anything else.

If you are curious about what IS happening in the World of Darkness, check
out the recently published clan novels... one for each clan starting with
Toreador. I was expecting them to be poorly written hack novels. I was
pleasantly surprised. They are well-written (mostly) and a lot of fun. Some
of the vampires from the Sabbat War set do indeed come from these books.
Moncada, Lucita, Sasha Vykos, Talley the Hound, Polonia, The Little Tailor
of Prague and a few others I think.

Cheers,
WES

Messages.Author: Andrew S. Davidson
Messages.Body:
On Fri, 22 Dec 2000 00:19:31 -0800, wes wrote:

>> It is relevant as long as it does not adversely affect the CCG. beyond
>> that the CCG comes first. When are people going to accept that
>
>I think the games should definitely be seperate entities BUT the World of
>Darkness that White Wolf created needs to be adhered to only because it is
>such a cool world.

Indeed. You make reference to storyline changes revealed in the clan
novels. I'd just note that the clan novels are not components for any
game but are fiction set in the common background. As such, they are
even more applicable to VTES than to VTM. In the RPG, a storyteller
would be expected to take the story in his own direction. In the CCG,
there is no such freedom and so it seems obvious that it should be
based on the canonical storyline rather than a storyline of its own.

>The changes in the meta-storyline that White Wolf has recently
>instituted, such as the Gangrel leaving the Camarilla
>(and now apparently some Assamites have joined it!)
>are interesting and definitely create possibilities for the cards.

Gangrel membership of the Camarilla is not defined by the cards but by
the rulebook. As and when a new rulebook appears, it could update the
clan's status accordingly.

Andrew

In article <3A42A924...@club-internet.fr>, Denis Tulbent

<dtul...@club-internet.fr> writes

>I do agree on this peculiar point. But your dismissing of the WoD as
>irrelevant in V:tES is innacceptable to me. This game is based on the WoD,
>and its mood should reflect the whole WoD pattern.

The only thing you can and should assume any player has knowledge of is
the rules.

If you start assuming that players also know the details of the WoD
backstory, even though that has never been released in any form of V:TES
product, you start introducing even more problems for those who work
simply on the rules. People who do not have access to large amounts of
V:tM material, to work such things out, would be denied from being able
to predict the outcome of any given situation. If you only use the game
rules, no player is adversely discriminated against. If they know the
rules of the game, they know the rules of the game. No other
information required.
